rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “God’s signs” broadly includes proofs of God’s existence and unity, revealed books, and miracles shown through prophets.
rows.anchor: “âyâtullah” Allah’ın varlığına ve birliğine ve herhangi bir husûsun hakkiyetine dair nasbettiği delâil

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The qualifier does not imply that some disputation without proof is acceptable; it warns that religious speech requires authority grounded in proof.
rows.anchor: burada “bigayri sultân” kaydının mefhûm-ı muhâlifi maksud değildir. Ancak din işinde söz söyleyebilmek için hüccet ve burhâna müstenid bir salâhiyet lâzım

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is also permissible to discuss divine signs by comparing them with other divine signs, as in abrogation, specification, and qualification.
rows.anchor: Bununla beraber nesih, tahsis ve takyid kabîlinden mesâilde olduğu gibi âyâtullahı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disputants’ pride is an unattainable claim to greatness: no one can rise above God’s signs or acquire a divinely withheld rank, such as prophethood.
rows.anchor: bir kibir ki[^3] onlar ona yetişecek değillerdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Everyone who argues against manifest truth from zealotry falls under this judgment, carrying an impossible pride in the heart.
rows.anchor: Delili zâhir olan hakka karşı taassub ile mücadele edenlerin hepsi bu hükümde dâhildir. Hepsi böyle sînelerinde yetişemeyecekleri bir kibir

rows.speaker: Kureyş müşrikleri
rows.claim: One reported occasion identifies the disputants as Quraysh idolaters, who objected that the Qur’an should have come to a great man from either town and that others had not preceded them in accepting it.
rows.anchor: Kureyş müşrikleridir ki[^4] لَوْلَا نُزِّلَ هَٰذَا ٱلْقُرْءَانُ عَلَىٰ رَجُلٍۢ مِّنَ

rows.speaker: Mukātil
rows.claim: Mukātil says the disputants were Jews who magnified the Dajjal; Abu al-Aliyah also adopted this identification.
rows.anchor: Mukātil demiştir ki “haklarında bu âyet nâzil olan mücâdiller Yahudîlerdir. Deccal’e tâzim ettiler, bu nâzil oldu.”

rows.speaker: Ebu’l- Âliye
rows.claim: Abu al-Aliyah likewise held that the verse concerned Jews who magnified the Dajjal.
rows.anchor: Ebu’l- Âliye de buna zâhib olmuştu.

rows.speaker: Âlûsî
rows.claim: Alusi cites Abd b. Humayd and Ibn Abi Hatim with a sound chain: Jews came to the Prophet and exalted the Dajjal’s future deeds; this account suits a Medinan dating for the verse.
rows.anchor: Âlûsî’nin nakline göre Abd b. Humeyd ve İbn Ebî Hâtim sened-i sahîh ile ondan şöyle tahrîc etmişlerdir

rows.speaker: Ebussuud
rows.claim: Abu al-Su‘ud reports that Jews claimed the Torah’s promised figure was not the Prophet but the Dajjal, whom they expected to rule land and sea and restore their sovereignty.
rows.anchor: Ebussuud bunu şöyle nakleder: “Bir de[^9] denildi ki mücadele edenler Yahudîlerdir. Diyorlardı ki ‘bizim Tevrat’ta mezkur olan

rows.speaker: Âlûsî
rows.claim: Alusi says the Jews lied both in denying the Prophet was their promised figure and in calling the Dajjal the son of David, since prophets warned against him as a trial, not good news.
rows.anchor: Âlûsî der ki: “Bu mücadelede Yehûd iki vechile yalan söylediler, evvelâ, Resûlullah’a ‘sen bizim muteber olan sâhibimiz değilsin’

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hadith reports name two eschatological Messiahs: Jesus’s descent and the Dajjal’s emergence.
rows.anchor: Hadis lerde eşrât-ı Sâ‘at’ten olmak üzere iki mesih zikrolunur. Birisi: Mesih Îsâ’nın nüzûlü

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports mention about thirty false claimants to prophethood, including Musaylima, and say the greatest Dajjal will emerge claiming divinity.
rows.anchor: Müseylime gibi yalan yere peygamberlik iddiasıyla çıkacak otuz kadar Deccal zikredilmiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı notes that Christians call Jesus the Messiah son of David, as Matthew does at the start of its Gospel.
rows.anchor: Matta İncili’nin başında görüldüğüne göre Hıristiyanlar bu ismi “Îse’l- Mesîh b. Dâvûd” diye Hazret-i Îsâ’ya vermektedirler.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Matthew traces Jesus’s Davidic lineage through Joseph despite saying Jesus was conceived before Mary and Joseph joined; Jews give the same title to the Dajjal, a curious shared viewpoint.
rows.anchor: Îsâ’nın tevellüdü Meryem’le Yûsuf’un ictimâ‘larından evvel Rûhu’l-Kudüs’ten oldu diye tasrih edilmiş iken Yûsuf babası imiş gibi onun vâsıtasıyla Hazret-i Dâvûd’a nisbet edilmesi bir tenakuz teşkil eder

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı glosses Messiah Dajjal as “false messiah”: a skilled deceiver whose unbelief is evident even as he performs wonders and claims divinity.
rows.anchor: Mesih-i Deccal yalancı mesih demektir. Vârid olan haberlere göre Deccal bir yalancı, nâsı aldatmakta mâhir bir sahtekârdır

rows.speaker: Ulemâ
rows.claim: Scholars argue God would not give a false prophet a miracle that could confirm his claim, since that would create doubt and lend proof to disputing God’s signs.
rows.anchor: Ulemâ demişlerdir ki: Allah teâlâ peygamberlik iddia eden bir yalancıya tasdik ihtimâli bulunan bir mucize vermez; çünkü teşkik olur

rows.speaker: Ulemâ
rows.claim: By contrast, scholars say God may allow wonders to a liar claiming divinity as a trial, because reason always shows that a created, originated being cannot be God.
rows.anchor: Fakat ulûhiyet iddia eden bir yalancıya ibtilâ için her türlü hârikayı verebilir. Zira kendisi hâdis olan mahlûkun Allah olmadığına aklî burhan dâima kāim

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Dajjal’s false-messiah identity signals that he will appear under imitation of Christianity.
rows.anchor: Deccal’in bu suretle bir yalancı mesih olması, onun Hıristiyanlık taklîdi altında zuhur edeceğini anlatır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports that the true Messiah Jesus will descend and kill the Dajjal support this interpretation.
rows.anchor: Mesîh-i sâdık olan Îsâ’nın nüzûlüyle onu katledeceğine dair olan eserler de bunu teyid eyler.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı condemns the Jews’ prideful hatred of Jesus and the final Prophet and their tragic hopes in the false messiah.
rows.anchor: mesîh-i sâdık olan Îsâ’ya ve Hâtemü’l-Enbiyâ’ya kibr ü hasetle küfrederek bütün ümitlerini mesîh-i kâzib olan Deccal’e bağlamaları

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He speculates whether England, which was then seeking to establish a Jewish government in Palestine, might play the role of the false messiah they awaited.
rows.anchor: gözledikleri mesîh-i kâzib rolünü oynayıverecek midir?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is told to seek God’s protection from pride, envious proud people, and the Dajjal’s evil.
rows.anchor: Onun için sen hemen Allah’a sığın öyle kibirden ve kibirli hasetçilerden, yahut Deccal’in şerrinden Allah’a sığın

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God hears every statement and sees every deed; the declaration is both a promise and a threat.
rows.anchor: bütün dediklerinizi işiten ve işitecek olan ve bütün yaptıklarınızı gören ve görecek olan ancak O’dur. Bu, bir taraftan vaad, bir taraftan va‘îddir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading rebukes human arrogance: people are tiny beside the heavens and earth, so it is ignorant to presume to be great against their Creator.
rows.anchor: bir kere nâsın[^20] Allah’a ve Allah’ın âyetlerine karşı kibr ü mücadelesi haddini bilmemek olduğunu ihtardır

rows.speaker: Zemahşerî
rows.claim: The verse can warn that creating the heavens and earth initially is greater than recreating people; therefore resurrection is certainly within God’s power. Zemakhshari prefers this reading.
rows.anchor: Zemahşerî bu mânayı tercih etmiştir.

rows.speaker: Nakkāş ve bazı müfessirler
rows.claim: Nakkash and some exegetes take “creation of people” as an agentive genitive: creating the heavens and earth exceeds what humans make, so human wonders cannot rival God’s creation.
rows.anchor: Nakkāş gibi bazı müfessirînin verdiği mânaya göre “halku’n-nâs” fâiline muzâf olmak üzere

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most people are deceived, either imagining themselves or their products greater than the heavens and earth, or human making greater than God’s making.
rows.anchor: Yahut insanların yaptığını Allah’ın yaptığından büyük zannederler, kibirlenirler.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The radio illustrates that people may mistake their invention for a greater craft than the ear, forgetting that radio depends on the ear and is itself created by God.
rows.anchor: radyoyu insanın halkı ve kulaktan daha mühim bir sanat zanneder

rows.speaker: Muhyiddîn-i Arabî
rows.claim: Ibn Arabi says the greatness here is not bodily size or quantity, but a divine meaning enacted in the heavens and earth that humans lack.
rows.anchor: Muhyiddîn-i Arabî Fütûhât-ı Mekkiyye’sinde der ki: “İşbu لَخَلْقُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ أَكْبَرُ مِنْ خَلْقِ ٱلنَّاسِ âyetinde büyüklüğü cirm ve kemmiyet büyüklüğü sanma

rows.speaker: Muhyiddîn-i Arabî
rows.claim: Ibn Arabi connects the trust in 33:72 with this greatness: bearing the trust entails risk and uncertainty, so the Qur’an calls humanity unjust and ignorant.
rows.anchor: belki emâneti hâmil olmak cehldendir, onun için Allah teâlâ ظَلُومًۭا جَهُولًۭا [el-Ahzâb 33/72]

rows.speaker: Muhyiddîn-i Arabî
rows.claim: Ibn Arabi says the heavens, earth, and mountains understood the trust’s gravity and risk and had more reason than humans in declining it.
rows.anchor: semâvât ve Arz ve cibâl emânetin kadrini ve onu hâmil olanın muhatarada olduğunu

rows.speaker: Muhyiddîn-i Arabî
rows.claim: Ibn Arabi links the cosmos’ response to God’s command in 41:13: when told to come willingly or unwillingly, heaven and earth answered in willing obedience.
rows.anchor: yani size bırakılacak şeyleri ister istemez kabûle âmâde olun dediği vakit

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı says Ibn Arabi’s account seems to conflict with his view of the human as a comprehensive microcosm; he reconciles them as bodily versus spiritual greatness, citing 45:13.
rows.anchor: Şeyhin bu sözü insanı nüsha-i kübrâ ve nüshâ-i câmi‘a addeden sözlerine münâfî görünür.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Physiologically, the cosmos never errs or disobeys God; though it did not voluntarily accept the trust, it faithfully safeguards what is imposed by necessity.
rows.anchor: Garîzî, yani fizyolojik haysiyetiyle bakıldığı zaman da semâvât ve Arz emr-i Hakk’a muhalif hiçbir şey yapmaz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humans err, disobey, and betray entrusted duties; in obedience to God’s command the heavens and earth are therefore greater than humans, exposing the ignorant pride of disputants.
rows.anchor: Hâlbuki insan hem hata eder hem isyan yapar, emânâtına zulüm de eder, yanılır da; bunun için semâvât ve Arz, Hakk’ın emrine itaat haysiyetiyle de insandan büyüktür

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The blind is the heart-blind person who fails to know truth at its beginning and end; the sighted is the person of learning and insight.
rows.anchor: Kör de gören ile müsâvî olmaz yani mebde’ ve me‘âdında hakkı tanımaz olan kör kalbli ile

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who know but do not act on their knowledge, or see yet pretend not to see, are also judged blind.
rows.anchor: İlmi olup da mûcebiyle amel etmeyenler, görüp de görmezceden gelenler de görmez hükmündedir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who believe and do righteous deeds are not equal to those who do evil.
rows.anchor: İman edip sâlih ameller işleyenlerle ne de kötülük yapan bunlar da müsâvî olmaz.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although humans are physically small, they can be the best of creation and a comprehensive copy through the heavens and earth being subjected to them, as 45:13 states.
rows.anchor: O hâlde insan ahsen-i takvîm de olur, cismânî olan küçüklüğe mukabil

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rebuke that people reflect very little is addressed either to humanity generally or to the disputants.
rows.anchor: ey insanlar yahut ey mücâdiller

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Hour, meaning the hour of judgment and resurrection, will certainly come, with no room for doubt.
rows.anchor: onda şüphe yok şüpheye mahal yok

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Despite the certainty of the Hour, most people do not believe.
rows.anchor: velâkin nâsın ekserîsi iman etmezler.

rows.speaker: Ibn Abbas, Dahhâk ve Mücâhid
rows.claim: One interpretation takes “call on Me” as worship Me and “I will answer” as grant reward; on this view, practical striving is also required.
rows.anchor: İbn Abbas, Dahhâk ve Mücâhid’den mervî olan

rows.speaker: Süddî
rows.claim: A second interpretation, transmitted from Suddi and apparent at first glance, is “ask Me and I will give you,” with worship then understood as prayer.
rows.anchor: ve ilk nazarda anlaşılan da budur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two readings emphasize that prayer and worship entail one another: prayer is worship’s core, while worship is among the conditions for prayer’s acceptance.
rows.anchor: Bunu böyle iki vecihli olarak ifadenin nüktesi, ibadetin dua

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to ask establishes particular human will and rejects compulsion; asking is a condition of God’s response, and abandoning the command incurs the threat of Hell.
rows.anchor: Gerek ibadet mânasına olsun gerek sade dua, ikisinde de istemek emredilmiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise does not mean every prayer is necessarily answered; acceptance is qualified by God’s will, as 6:41 states.
rows.anchor: meşiyyet ile mukayyeddir. Yani buradan anlaşılan kaziyye-i şartiye külliye değil mühmeledir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The condition is not a universally quantified promise, and acceptance also depends on conditions such as good words and righteous deeds in 35:10.
rows.anchor: Müeddâsınca bazı şerâit-i kabul ile de meşruttur.

rows.speaker: Ka‘b
rows.claim: Al-Kashshaf transmits Ka‘b’s report that this community received three privileges: witness over humanity, freedom from hardship, and the promise “call on Me and I will answer,” linked to 2:143, 33:38, and 5:6.
rows.anchor: Keşşâf da Ka‘b’dan şöyle nakleder: Allah teâlâ bu ümmete üç haslet vermiştir ki onları nebiyy-i mürsel olanlardan başkasına vermemişti

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Call Me” may mean seek Me from Me: God answers by being found, and whoever finds God has found everything, since all things obey His creative command in 36:82.
rows.anchor: Benden Beni talep edin, size icâbet ederim, Beni bulursunuz, Beni bulan da her şeyi bulmuş olur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı says this God-seeking prayer is described as never rejected, and cites a report meaning “whoever seeks Me finds Me.”
rows.anchor: Denilmiştir ki işte hiç reddolunmayan dua budur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who arrogantly refuse worship or seeking God through prayer remain humiliated and deprived in the Hell of separation from Him.
rows.anchor: Bana ibadetten, yani Bana dua ile Beni

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God commands people in every age and community to unite in upholding the religion, meaning the law revealed for their time, without splitting over it.
rows.anchor: dini ki o her zaman ve millette vaktin şer‘idir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He invokes the saying that God’s hand is with the community and the image of a wolf taking the sheep that separates from its flock.
rows.anchor: Kurt da sürüden ayrılan koyunu yer

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is conceived as the one worthy of worship through His beautiful names; their multiplicity accompanies, rather than negates, unity of the divine essence.
rows.anchor: Onun için esmâsının kesreti ile beraber aynını tevhid lâzımdır.

rows.speaker: Hukemâdan birisi
rows.claim: A dying sage showed his children that a bundled sheaf of sticks could not be broken together, but the separated sticks broke one by one, illustrating the strength of unity.
rows.anchor: Hukemâdan birisi vefat ederken evlâdına vasiyet etti bir cemaat idiler, ‘bana bir kucak değnek getirin’ dedi getirdiler.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Likewise, those who unite in establishing the religion cannot be overcome by an enemy, while division gives the enemy an opening to destroy them.
rows.anchor: İkāme-i din hususunda ictimâ‘edip de dağılmadıkları takdirde düşman onlara kahredemez.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same applies inwardly: when someone gathers their resolve to uphold God’s religion, devils from humans or jinn cannot defeat them against the aid of faith and the angels.
rows.anchor: Nefsinde kendini toplayıp da Allah’ın dinini ikāmeye azmettiği vakit ne insten ne cinden bir şeytan vereceği vesvese ile onu imanın ve melekin müsâ‘adesi karşısında mağlup edemez.
